function.name: add_comment
function.description: Leave a comment on a task. This is how progress and findings are recorded.

function.name: agent_connections
function.description:
The connection log: every attempt to connect, accepted or refused.

        This is how an agent that never shows up in list_agents is diagnosed -
        a rejected attempt (a stale token, a misconfigured container) is
        logged here with the reason it was turned away, even though it never
        became an agent. Narrow to one agent by id or unambiguous name, or
        leave it unset to see every agent's log.

function.name: assign_task
function.description:
Say who a task is for; omit assignee to clear it.

        Not the same as claiming it. A claim says "I have this right now" and
        moves the task to in_progress; an assignee says "this is yours to pick
        up", changes no status and takes no lock, so work that has not started
        does not look underway. A person is a bare name, an agent writes itself
        as agent:<name> - the same convention the author field uses.

function.name: claim_task
function.description:
Take a task so another agent will not pick it up, moving it to in_progress.

        Fails if someone else holds it, naming the holder; force steals the lock.

function.name: create_document
function.description:
Create an adr/prd/technical_design/proposal from a body or a repo file.

        Give exactly one of body (inline markdown) or file_path (relative to the
        project's repo_root).

function.name: create_project
function.description:
Create a project. repo_root is the checkout its documents live in.

        parent nests it inside another project - a workspace holding one
        project per git repo, which is how several related repos are tracked
        together.

function.name: create_pull_request
function.description:
Push the current branch and open a pull request, returning its URL.

        Write title and body yourself - you are the model, taskq is not. Omit
        both and gh fills them from the branch's commit messages.

function.name: create_task
function.description:
Create a task, optionally as a subtask of parent.

        A parent must be in the same project. branch associates the task with a
        git branch. priority is low/medium/high/urgent, severity minor/major/critical.

function.name: delete_comment
function.description: Delete one comment. Nothing cascades; restore_comment brings it back.

function.name: delete_document
function.description: Delete one document. Nothing cascades; restore_document brings it back.

function.name: delete_task
function.description:
Delete a task together with its subtasks and their comments.

        Nothing is erased: the rows are hidden from every listing, read, and
        search, the event log keeps the whole record, and restore_task puts
        back exactly what this call hid. Say why in reason.

function.name: get_document
function.description: Show one document with its body (or repo file reference) and relations.

function.name: get_handoff
function.description:
A project's current handoff, and the tasks it points at.

        Worth reading before starting work: it is the last agent's account of
        where things are, which the task list does not carry.

function.name: get_project
function.description: Show one project (by name or id) and its top-level tasks.

function.name: get_task
function.description: Show one task with its subtasks, relations, comments, and recent events.

function.name: git_push
function.description: Push the project's current branch, setting upstream on first push.

function.name: git_push_all
function.description: Push every branch of the project's repo to its remote.

function.name: git_status
function.description:
The git state of every repo in a project: branch, tracking,
        working-tree changes, and the last commit with the files it touched.

        Returns {"repos": [...]}, one entry per repo, named by the project that
        owns it - a workspace holding several repos reports all of them.

function.name: link_nodes
function.description:
Record a relation: blocked_by, requires, documented_by, or references.

        Informational only - nothing blocks a status change on it - but it is
        what get_task surfaces as a task's prerequisites and design docs.

function.name: list_agents
function.description:
List the tq agents that have ever connected, most recently seen first.

        online_only restricts the list to agents currently connected. Each
        entry carries id, name, host, cwd, task_id, status, claude_pid,
        last_seen_at, and restarts.

function.name: list_comments
function.description: List a task's comments, oldest first.

function.name: list_deleted
function.description:
List what has been deleted: the trash, most recently deleted first.

        Each entry carries its kind (task/comment/document), id, label, when it
        was deleted, by whom, and the reason given. kind and project narrow it.

function.name: list_documents
function.description:
List documents, optionally by project or type (adr, prd,
        technical_design, proposal). A project covers the projects inside it.

function.name: list_events
function.description: Read the append-only event history, newest first.

function.name: list_projects
function.description: List every project with its task count.

function.name: list_tasks
function.description:
List tasks as a flat array; nest them yourself via parent_id.

        status filters to any of the given statuses (todo, in_progress, blocked,
        done, cancelled). parent lists one task's direct children. recent orders
        by most recent status change instead of manual order. A project holding
        other projects lists theirs too (each row carries its project_id);
        children=False lists that project's own tasks only. assignee filters to
        what one person or agent has been given; "none" finds the unassigned.

function.name: pr_status
function.description:
The pull request for the current branch (or a given number/URL):
        state, review decision, merge status, and URL.

function.name: project_status
function.description:
A project's status: what is in progress, recently closed, and next up.

        The best first call for "where does this project stand", cheaper to read
        than listing every task. A project holding other projects reports for
        all of them; children=False narrows it to this project alone.

function.name: release_task
function.description: Release a task's claim, leaving its status alone.

function.name: restart_agent
function.description:
Restart one connected agent, named by id or by unambiguous name.

        The id is stable across reconnects and disconnects - it is the
        reliable way to name one - while a name is refused when more than one
        agent shares it. Blocks until the agent answers (up to the hub's own
        timeout) and fails if it is not currently online.

function.name: restart_server
function.description:
Restart the taskq frontends so code changes on the host take effect.

        Call this after editing taskq's own source. target is all, mcp or slack
        - use mcp to leave the Slack connection alone. This answers before the
        restart happens (about a second beforehand): `taskq serve` holds the
        listening socket, so your next call lands on the new process with
        nothing to reconnect.

        The whole thing takes a few seconds: the children are stopped, a quiet
        window passes so requests drain and Slack drops the old connection, and
        then they start. Calling again during that window is refused rather
        than queued - wait and check server_status instead. Fails if no
        `taskq serve` is running.

function.name: restore_comment
function.description: Restore a deleted comment.

function.name: restore_document
function.description: Restore a deleted document.

function.name: restore_task
function.description:
Restore a deleted task, undoing exactly what its own delete hid.

        A subtask deleted separately beforehand stays deleted; restore it by id.

function.name: search_taskq
function.description:
Find tasks, comments, and documents by describing them.

        Use this when the user refers to work by what it is about ("the ticket
        about slow page loads") instead of by id. Ranks by meaning and keyword
        match together; kinds restricts to task/comment/document, statuses to
        tasks in those statuses. A project covers the projects inside it unless
        children is False.

function.name: server_status
function.description: Show the running taskq serve: pids, port, uptime and restart count.

function.name: set_handoff
function.description:
Replace a project's handoff with where things stand right now.

        A few lines saying where you are and what you have done, for whoever
        picks this up next - it is read at a glance, so keep it short. The
        handoff it replaces is kept but no longer shown. tasks links the ones
        it refers to; task says which single task it is about.

function.name: set_task_status
function.description:
Move a task to todo/in_progress/blocked/done/cancelled.

        Leaving in_progress requires a comment explaining the transition; the
        comment is recorded against the task alongside the status event.

function.name: set_task_summary
function.description:
Set a task's short summary; omit summary to clear it.

        A few lines saying what the task is actually about, so somebody can
        decide what to look at without reading a description that runs to
        pages. Keep it short and concrete; nothing generates it for you.

function.name: task_queue
function.description:
What to pick up next: unclaimed todo tasks, highest priority first.

        Every project unless you name one. This is project_status's "next up"
        section on its own - the right call when you are looking for work
        rather than reporting on a project. assignee narrows it to what one
        person or agent has been given, turning "what is going spare" into
        "what should I be doing"; "none" asks for the unassigned.

function.name: task_summaries
function.description:
Open tasks with their summaries, highest priority first.

        missing=True returns only the ones nobody has summarised yet, which is
        what a summarising pass asks for.

function.name: task_to_issue
function.description:
Open a GitHub issue for a task and record the issue number+URL on it.

        The issue goes to the task's project repo. A task already linked to an
        issue is refused rather than opening a duplicate.

function.name: unlink_nodes
function.description: Remove a relation previously recorded by link_nodes.

function.name: update_document
function.description: Update a document. Setting body clears file_path and vice versa.

function.name: update_project
function.description:
Update a project's description, repo_root or parent.

        Omitted fields are kept; parent "0" moves the project back to the top
        level.

function.name: update_task
function.description:
Update a task's fields. Omitted fields are left alone; parent=0 detaches.

        project moves the task to another project, taking its subtasks with it
        - which is how a task lands in the child project that owns its repo.
